summary: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.
Count forward starting from any given number, not just 1.
Write numbers 0 to 20 and use a numeral to show how many objects.
Connect counting to quantity: one number per object, last number tells how many, next is one more.
Count up to 20 objects in a line, array or circle (10 scattered); count out a given number.
Compare two groups of up to 10 objects: greater than, less than, or equal.
Compare two written numbers between 0 and 10.
Show addition and subtraction with concrete objects and actions.
Solve addition and subtraction word problems within 10 using objects or drawings.
Break numbers up to 10 into pairs in more than one way and record them.
Find the number that makes 10 with a given number from 1 to 9.
Add and subtract within 5 fluently.
Show numbers 11 to 19 as ten ones and some more ones.
Show understanding of adding and subtracting within 10 using place value ideas.
Describe things about an object that can be measured, like length or weight.
Directly compare two objects to see which has more or less of an attribute.
Sort objects into categories, count each category (up to 10) and order categories by count.
Name shapes around you and describe positions with words like above, below, beside, behind.
Name shapes in any size or orientation, including rhombus and trapezoid.
Tell whether a shape is flat (two-dimensional) or solid (three-dimensional).
Compare 2-D and 3-D shapes by sides, corners and other features in informal language.
Build and draw shapes found in the world.
Put simple shapes together to make larger shapes.
Solve add and subtract word problems within 20 with the unknown in any position.
Solve word problems adding three whole numbers with a sum up to 20.
Use commutative and associative properties as strategies to add and subtract within 20.
Treat subtraction as finding a missing addend.
Link counting to adding and subtracting, such as counting on 2 to add 2.
Fluently add and subtract within 10 (CCSS also asks for strategies within 20).
Understand the equal sign and decide if addition and subtraction equations are true or false.
Find the missing whole number in an addition or subtraction equation.
Count to 120 by 1s, 2s and 10s from any number under 100; read and write numerals.
Know two-digit numbers are made of tens and ones, including teen numbers and decades.
Compare two two-digit numbers using tens and ones and the symbols >, =, <.
Add within 100 (two-digit plus one-digit or a multiple of ten) using models and place value.
Mentally find 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number.
Subtract multiples of 10 from multiples of 10 within 10 to 90 using models and strategies.
Order three objects by length and compare two lengths using a third object.
Measure length by laying copies of a shorter unit end to end with no gaps.

Organize and read data with up to three categories; answer how many and how many more.

Combine 2-D or 3-D shapes to make composite shapes and new shapes from them.
Split circles and rectangles into halves and fourths and name the shares.
Solve one- and two-step add and subtract word problems within 100.
Add and subtract within 20 fluently; know all single-digit sums from memory.
Decide if a group of up to 20 objects is odd or even (no doubles equation).
Use repeated addition to find the total in arrays up to 5 by 5.
Know three-digit numbers are hundreds, tens and ones; 100 is ten tens.
Count within 1000 and skip-count by 5s, 10s and 100s.
Read and write numbers to 1000 in numerals, words and expanded form.
Compare two three-digit numbers using place value and >, =, <.
Add and subtract within 100 fluently using place value strategies.
Add up to three two-digit numbers (CCSS: four) using place value and properties.
Add and subtract within 1000 with models and place value, regrouping when needed.
Mentally add or subtract 10 or 100 for numbers from 100 to 900.
Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work using place value and properties.
Measure length with tools like rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks and tapes.
Measure one object with two different units and relate the results to unit size.
Estimate lengths in inches, feet, centimeters and meters.
Measure how much longer one object is than another in standard units.
Solve add and subtract word problems within 100 about lengths.
Show whole numbers, sums and differences within 100 on a number line.
Tell and write time to the nearest five minutes with a.m. and p.m.
Solve word problems with dollar bills and coins using $ and cent symbols.
Measure several objects to the nearest unit and show the data on a line plot.
Make picture and bar graphs with up to four categories and solve problems from them.
Describe 2-D and 3-D shapes by faces, angles, sides and vertices; draw 2-D shapes.
Split a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size rectangles and count them.
Split circles and rectangles into halves, thirds or fourths; equal shares can differ in shape.

Understand division as sharing into equal groups or finding the number of groups.
Solve multiplication and division word problems within 100 with groups, arrays and measures.
Find the missing number in a multiplication or division equation.
Use commutative, associative and distributive properties to multiply and divide.
Treat division as finding an unknown factor.

Solve two-step word problems with the four operations, using equations and order of operations.
Find patterns in addition and multiplication tables and explain them with properties.
Check answers for reasonableness with mental math and estimation, including rounding.
Round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.
Add and subtract within 1000 fluently.
Multiply one-digit numbers by multiples of 10 such as 9 x 80.

Find area by counting unit squares.

Round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.
Add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers fluently with the standard algorithm.
Multiply up to four digits by one digit and two digits by two digits.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by one-digit numbers, with remainders.

Compare fractions with different numerators and denominators.

Multiply a fraction by a whole number, including word problems.
Rewrite tenths as hundredths and add tenths and hundredths.
Write tenths and hundredths as decimals and place them on a number line.

Solve word problems with distance, time, volume, mass and money.
Use area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in problems.
Make line plots of fraction measurements and solve problems from them.
Understand angles and degree measure as parts of a circle.
Measure and sketch angles with a protractor.
Add angle measures and find unknown angles.
Draw and identify points, lines, segments, rays, angles, perpendicular and parallel lines.

Find and draw lines of symmetry.

Divide up to four-digit numbers by two-digit numbers.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals to hundredths.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with unlike denominators.
Solve fraction add and subtract word problems and check reasonableness with benchmarks.
Understand a fraction as division and solve sharing problems with fraction answers.
Multiply fractions by whole numbers and fractions, including area with fractional sides.

Solve real-world problems multiplying fractions and mixed numbers.
Divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions.
Convert between units within one measurement system and use them in multi-step problems.
Make line plots of fraction measurements and solve problems with them.
Understand volume as filling a solid with unit cubes.
Find volume by counting unit cubes.
Find volumes of rectangular prisms with formulas and add volumes of combined prisms.
Understand the coordinate plane: axes, origin and ordered pairs.
Graph points in the first quadrant to solve problems.
Know attributes of a shape category belong to all its subcategories.
Classify 2-D figures in a hierarchy by properties.

state_code: # - Arizona Mathematics Standards, adopted by the State Board of Education Dec 2016 (still the current K-5 standards for 2026-27; the
#   2025 ADE grade documents say "Adopted December 2016, Updated 1-29-2025" and only add AASA Essential Standards marks).
# - azed.gov and cms.azed.gov return a Cloudflare challenge (403) to scripted fetches, so the official ADE PDFs were read from Internet Archive copies:
# - Official comparison: "2016 Math K-5 Red-line Standards" (draft-to-final redline with reviewer notes, not a direct CCSS table):
# - CCSS links here are judged by comparing AZ text with CCSS text.
# - Grade.Domain.Cluster.Standard like CCSS (e.g. 1.MD.B.3b). Sub-parts that restate CCSS sub-parts are folded.
# - Separately coded splits kept as rows: 1.MD.B.3a (time) / 1.MD.B.3b (coins), 3.MD.A.1a (time) / 3.MD.A.1b (money).
#   The 2025 grade-3 document prints 3.MD.A.1 with a./b. parts instead of separate codes; the 2016/2018 codes are used.
# - Added standards take new numbers: K.NBT.B.2, 3.OA.D.10, 4.OA.C.6, 5.OA.B.4.
# - Code differs for the same content: AZ 3.MD.C.8 = CCSS 3.MD.D.8 (perimeter moved into cluster C).
# - The kindergarten PDF prints the OA codes with a zero ("K.0A.A.1"); written here as K.OA.
# - None dropped as a whole. Parts dropped: 4.OA.B.4 prime/composite (moved to AZ 5.OA.B.4) and "multiple of a given one-digit number";
#   5.NBT.A.2 whole-number exponents for powers of 10; 2.OA.C.3 equation for even numbers as doubles; 1.OA.C.6 within-20 strategies
#   (AZ 1.OA.C cluster is "within 10"); 2.NBT.B.6 four addends cut to three; 4.OA.C.5 shape patterns.
# - Estimation checks in 3.OA.D.8 and 4.OA.A.3 were split out as AZ 3.OA.D.10 and 4.OA.C.6 (mapped back to those CCSS codes).
# - New: K.NBT.B.2 (add and subtract within 10 using place value).
# - Earlier than CCSS: coin names and values in grade 1 (1.MD.B.3b); money to $20.00 with decimal notation in grade 3 (3.MD.A.1b);
#   converting smaller units to larger in grade 4 (4.MD.A.1); skip counting by 2s and 10s in grade 1 (1.NBT.A.1).
# - Later than CCSS: primes and prime factorization in grade 5 (5.OA.B.4; prime factorization itself is CCSS 6.NS.B.4, outside K-5).
# - Small additions inside matched standards: remainder as a fraction of the divisor (4.OA.A.3), "unit fraction" term (3.NF.A.2c),
#   rhombus/trapezoid in K (K.G.A.2), quarter-inch measuring (3.MD.B.4), 0 to 10 comparisons (K.CC.C.7).
# - K-2 2025-updated documents were not available (not archived); the 2018-updated K-2 PDFs were used. Grades 3-5 2025 and 2018 texts agree.
# - No newer adopted Arizona math standards were found for 2026-27; ADE grade documents updated in 2025 still carry the 2016 standards.
# - 3.MD.A.1b mapped to both 2.MD.C.8 (bills and coins) and 4.MD.A.2 (money with decimals).
# - 3.OA.D.10 and 4.OA.C.6 marked same: their content is the estimation sentence of CCSS 3.OA.D.8 / 4.OA.A.3.
# - kind is judged on content: same = CCSS content with only rewording, examples or limits that CCSS also implies.
